# What this page is

RAG is how you give a frozen language model fresh, inspectable evidence: retrieve a passage, put it in the prompt, and then generate. The full reader's guides, drawn from CS 329Z Lecture 3, are:

- [Why RAG](/rag/why-rag.qmd) — why retrieve, and the shape of the loop
- [Indexing for RAG](/rag/rag-indexing.qmd) — chunking, contextual retrieval, and the index
- [Retrievers for RAG](/rag/rag-retrieval.qmd) — BM25, DPR, and ColBERT
- [Agentic RAG](/rag/agentic-rag.qmd) — when retrieval is an action
- [Failure modes of RAG](/rag/rag-failure-modes.qmd)

RAG is also named in the comparison table on the [Generative AI overview](generative-index.qmd), and as a compound pattern on [Compound AI systems](/rag/compound-ai-systems.qmd).
